races.name: Westcare Home Care Claiming Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bryson
runners_data.note: OR 96, trainer W R Crawford with 0/2 in the past 14 days; races from the back and will be further behind than he wants given the hold-up traffic — 23 days since last run with a form string of B6-U26 that screams inconsistency, and the 7lb claim of Joshua Halford may not compensate for the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but a runner-up two starts back shows the ability is there; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 23 days between runs leaves him fresh, though 162 lb is a stern burden to carry.

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old for Mark McNiff wearing a tongue-strap, and although he showed a placed effort (2nd) on Good over 16f, he hasn't run in 37 days and returns with a form string of P-920P — his natural rear-of-field preference will be squeezed by the crowded hold-up pack, making his route to the front extremely difficult.
runners_data.comment: Presenting Lad arrives 37 days fresh and has run over today's trip and going, but he's winless in his last five starts, and a pulled up on his latest outing followed by an unplaced effort make it hard to fancy him despite the second three starts back suggesting residual ability.

runners_data.name: Raydamann
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old bounced back to winning ways over 18f on Good (1st, LR 26 days) and is the only horse mapped on the lead — he's a natural prominent/hold-up type asked to front-run, so his effort last time at this trip on identical going is the key form reference, and James Smith's 5lb claim keeps the weight competitive at 162lbs.
runners_data.comment: Raydamann brings a recent win to the table and has run over today's trip and going, with 26 days since that victory keeping him fresh; the chief concern is his trainer's deeply poor current strike rate of just one winner from 44 runners over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Tonguetie and blinkers for Karl Thornton's nine-year-old who won over 17f on Good and placed on the same surface — OR 114 is the second-highest in the field, Ben Harvey takes the ride, and though he's a natural hold-up horse who'll be shuffled into the midfield pack, his tactical versatility and good-ground form make him one of the most interesting runners in the race.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Rich Belief arrives here on a sharp 25-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on; carrying 162 lb is the one query, but his rating of 123 marks him as the clear class act in this field.

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's seven-year-old holds the highest OR in the field at 120 but returns from a string of disappointing flat efforts (form 00/R6-) and steps markedly up in trip from 12f to 18f; wears a tongue-strap, and Daniel King rides — the class level is enticing but the recent form gives little confidence.
runners_data.comment:
I cannot make a positive case for God Of Thunder as a strong threat — his recent form shows a sixth, a refusal, and two unplaced efforts in his last four starts, which offers no credible foundation for presenting him as a leading danger without inventing claims the facts don't support.

If you'd like, I can write an honest, balanced comment reflecting his actual profile instead.

runners_data.name: Warm In Gorey
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's eight-year-old wears a hood and has posted consecutive placed efforts on Good ground (3rd twice in last two completed runs) — 35 days since last run, OR 97, and Mr R Sugrue's 7lb claim helps at 152lbs; a natural hold-up type whose late finishing run will be compressed by the midfield bottleneck, though his stamina credentials over this sort of trip are genuine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of ten on our figures, Warm In Gorey faces a stiff task at 152 lb, though two thirds in recent starts and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's seven-year-old has a 1W4P record on similar going and steps down from 20-24f, which should suit the 18f trip here — OR 115, wears tongue-tie and blinkers, Josh Williamson claims 5lbs, and form of P-48F0 includes a fall; jumping must be clean but the class at this level is solid.
runners_data.comment: Howdoyalikeherhome has run over today's trip and going, and at 146 lb his weight burden isn't extreme for a mark of 115 — yet he's winless in his last five starts, and a trainer strike-rate of just 2% over the past fortnight is the real concern.

runners_data.name: Oh So Charming
runners_data.note: Declan Queally's six-year-old wearing a tongue-strap, with Kevin Healy's 7lb claim reducing the weight to 146lbs — OR 95, form 4-5250 includes a second on Good over 17f, and an excellent 14/15 sim-going record suggests the surface is not a concern; as one of several hold-up types mapped into midfield, the tactical ask is significant.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Oh So Charming looks hard to fancy here; a second three starts back offers slim encouragement, but an unplaced effort last time and 146 lb to carry make him a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Slowdownbarney
runners_data.note: Dermot McLoughlin's five-year-old who has never won or placed in five recorded runs and sports a tongue-tie and visor — OR 88 is lowest in the race, form of 8/080 is modest, and only 4/15 similar-going entries suggest the surface may not play to his strengths; P J O'Hanlon takes the ride and an outside draw compounds an already difficult task.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and lightly raced, Slowdownbarney is yet to score in recent starts but remains open to improvement, and 31 days between runs leaves him fresh enough to strip fitter here carrying 146 lb.

runners_data.name: Truckers Cruising
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's eight-year-old who returned just nine days ago (form U6-0P0), is wearing a tongue-strap, and has shown nothing in 11/13 finishes on Good going — OR 92, Sam Ewing rides, and a 0W0P record on similar going makes this a very hard proposition; the short turnaround and uninspiring recent efforts suggest this is a run for fitness rather than victory.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — a run that includes a pull-up and an unseating — Truckers Cruising faces a stiff task here, with a struggling trainer (1 from 44 in the past fortnight) adding little encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going, at least.

races.paceDynamic: Raydamann is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 10-runner claiming hurdle and will likely set off in front from flag to finish, creating a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good ground at Sligo — a tight, turning track that rewards jumping fluency and position. With no other genuine front-runner to press him, James Smith (5lb claim) can dictate a measured gallop, making this a race run predominantly to suit horses who can race prominently or track the leader into the straight. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Rich Belief, Presenting Lad, Warm In Gorey, Oh So Charming, Slowdownbarney, Bryson, and Truckers Cruising all prefer to come from off the pace, but the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear, meaning several will be shuffled into a midfield pack wider than their ideal. Given the uncontested lead and a track where kickbacks from a tight-bunched midfield make ground-making harder, this race shape strongly favours horses that can track Raydamann in second or third — horses racing close to the controllable pace will have the clearest view at every hurdle and the shortest route home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Raydamann Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Raydamann bowls along unchallenged and the hold-up pack cannot close the gap over the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Raydamann sets a comfortable, energy-conserving tempo with no rival willing to go with him, meaning his rivals must produce sustained late momentum on a track that blunts long finishing runs; his recent win over 18f on Good and Gordon Elliott's T14 form make this the default shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned second or third throughout tracks Raydamann closely and outstays him from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The steady early gallop means the lead is accessible for any runner prepared to sit just off Raydamann's shoulder, and Good ground keeps the finish honest rather than grinding; God Of Thunder, despite disappointing flat form, steps back up in trip here and Daniel King can press from off the early pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If Raydamann sets a fraction too strong early and weakens after the last, gifting a late closer a rare opportunity.
scenarios.body: Should Raydamann over-extend himself on a sharp Sligo track, one of the better-credentialed hold-up horses — Rich Belief (1W2P on Good, OR 114) or Warm In Gorey (back-to-back thirds on Good) — could swoop late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrum Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, interference in the bunched midfield pack, or a loose horse disrupts the race and hands it to a fluent jumper from mid-division.
scenarios.body: With seven horses effectively crowded into a midfield band at a tight, undulating track, one fall or clumsy jump could reshuffle the order dramatically; Howdoyalikeherhome, a previous winner on Good (11W4P sim-going), has the jumping class to profit from such chaos.

watchPoints.text: Raydamann has no front-runner to test him but is a natural hold-up type asked to make all — if he jumps untidily or idles in front, the horse immediately tracking him (likely God Of Thunder or Rich Belief) could steal first run at the last.

With seven runners effectively bundled into a midfield pack on a tight Sligo track, watch for early crowding at the first two hurdles — any jumping mistake from Slowdownbarney or Truckers Cruising could cause interference that disrupts Rich Belief or Warm In Gorey's race before it begins.

God Of Thunder's trip up from 12f to 18f is a significant jump — if he travels well early under Daniel King but fails to stay the final climb, he could stop quickly and bring down a rival jumping the last.

Warm In Gorey and Oh So Charming both carry 7lb claims (Mr R Sugrue and Kevin Healy respectively) — if either claim proves decisive in a tight finish, the weight advantage from the lowest-rated riders in the race could be the marginal edge in what may be a slowly-run finish.

Gordon Elliott saddles three runners (Raydamann, Howdoyalikeherhome, Truckers Cruising) with a T14 of 1/44 — watch which of the three is ridden to win versus ridden for place or fitness, as stable tactics could significantly influence how the midfield shapes up from the third-last hurdle.

races.name: Martin Reilly Hyundai Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: An Lachin Beag
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 6-year-old returning after 223 days off but with a solid Good-ground hurdle placing on record; Paddy Cleary (7lb claimer) takes the ride for Nigel Slevin and the fresher horse angle makes the long layoff a double-edged sword — fitness is the only real concern.

runners_data.name: Circus Hill
runners_data.note: Good-ground specialist with five consecutive placings at this trip and trip range, all on Good; a natural hold-up horse whose true style is compromised in this pace-heavy field, likely to race more prominently than ideal, which tempers confidence despite the consistent form.

runners_data.name: Glendaars Crystal
runners_data.note: Three Good-ground runs at maiden hurdle level with finishes of 9th, 11th and 7th — the fade flag is consistent and telling; the redistribution into midfield from a natural hold-up position means this horse is unlikely to find the finish position its style demands.

runners_data.name: I Dont Really Care
runners_data.note: Sole career run produced a 14th on Soft ground, 229 days ago — stamina for Good ground is unproven and the hold-up style being squeezed into a midfield slot by the crowded rear of the field undermines any case; hard to support on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Idaho Expresso
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with tongue-tie and headgear, and a persistent fade in recent form including a pulled-up run; the contest with Speisialta for the lead is likely to find Idaho Expresso out if the pace becomes genuinely honest over Sligo's 2m2f.

runners_data.name: Nelliestar
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose entire career history is on Flat or AW surfaces — all five runs came on Tapeta or Standard, and jumping hurdles on turf Good ground is a completely new environment; the hold-up style and the fade flag make this a very difficult race to assess positively.

runners_data.name: Saoirses Choice
runners_data.note: 4th on Soft and 9th on Good in two hurdle starts, with the 4th on softer ground the most encouraging; hold-up style will be squeezed in this field but the 60-day freshener and 7lb claimer Alix Balfe keep costs low if support emerges.

runners_data.name: Sea Feliz
runners_data.note: Debut tenth over this exact trip on Good ground for the dominant W P Mullins/Danny Mullins combination — the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 17/60 is the most significant context here, and the market on raceday should be monitored closely for intent even if the form is bare.

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning just 14 days after her last run, with tongue-tie applied; faces a direct duel with Idaho Expresso but if she can see that rival off early, her stamina for 2m2f and Eoin Staples' 5lb allowance give her a realistic chance of controlling this race.

runners_data.name: Kilgharrahs Love
runners_data.note: 4-year-old with a modest record mostly on Soft and AW surfaces; a genuine hold-up type whose best form came over shorter trips, and being mapped into midfield by a crowded rear means the tactical scenario does not naturally align with how this horse wants to race.

runners_data.name: Maroel
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity — no form string, no history provided, 4-year-old for Maike Magnussen with Conor Clarke (7lb claimer); the UNKNOWN going style means any assessment is speculative and the market is the only guide.

runners_data.name: Moonwing
runners_data.note: 4-year-old with one run to her name — an 11th on Good over 2m1f; the fade flag from that debut and a hold-up style in a field where the rear is crowded make meaningful improvement hard to project without a significant step forward.

runners_data.name: My Elusive Mate
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 4-year-old with back-to-back 5th and 7th placings over 2m on Good ground — the form is modest but the prominent style is exactly right for this pace shape, and Elliott's 14-day record of 1/44 is low, but Sam Ewing takes the ride in what looks a winnable maiden.

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta and Idaho Expresso are the two confirmed front-runners in this 13-runner mares maiden, and with both holding headgear (hurdles tongue-ties) and clear front-running profiles, a contested early pace is virtually certain on Good ground at Sligo's compact track. Idaho Expresso carries a fade flag from recent form, meaning Speisialta — ridden by the 5lb claimer Eoin Staples — is most likely to dominate from the front if Idaho Expresso cannot sustain the early duel. The honest gallop this creates over 2m2f on Good ground will suit horses that can travel prominently off the pace and pick up into the straight, rather than those requiring a late surge from the rear. This field holds more hold-up types than the track can accommodate at the rear — Kilgharrahs Love, I Dont Really Care, Glendaars Crystal and Circus Hill are all genuine hold-up horses that will be forced to race in a more prominent position than suits them naturally; An Lachin Beag and My Elusive Mate are the prominent types best placed to exploit the pace scenario as it develops. The race shape decisively favours prominent racers who can track the front-runners and produce a sustained run from two out, with true closers disadvantaged by being unable to find their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta and Idaho Expresso fight for the lead and set a true honest gallop, leaving the prominent chasers to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: The front pair burn each other off over the final circuit and a horse tracking in second or third position has enough energy left to assert from the second-last hurdle home; Good ground at Sligo rewards this profile as the track's tight bends punish late closers. An Lachin Beag and My Elusive Mate are best placed tactically to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Speisialta Dominates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Idaho Expresso fades or fails to press from the front, leaving Speisialta to control a moderate tempo alone.
scenarios.body: Speisialta dictates an uncontested gallop, conserves energy jumping and quickens clear before the last, turning this into a test of jumping accuracy rather than stamina; the fade flag on Idaho Expresso makes this a genuine possibility given recent form. Speisialta's hurdling (tongue-tie) will be the key variable in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Exploit Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stop the front pair cold and create a falsely run final circuit.
scenarios.body: Circus Hill has consistent form at this trip on Good ground with three placed efforts in similar conditions, and if chaos at the front creates a gap, she is the best credentialled of the hold-up types — though her redistribution into midfield makes this harder to deliver than her form suggests. Glendaars Crystal and I Dont Really Care share this profile but carry fade flags that undermine their claims.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mullins Newcomer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Feliz, trained by W P Mullins and having learned from her debut run, produces a significant step forward in this weaker maiden.
scenarios.body: W P Mullins' operation sends a 17/60 14-day strike rate to the table and Sea Feliz — a 5-year-old with only one run behind her — could be a completely different proposition second time; however, her debut was a distant tenth over the same 2m2f trip on Good ground, and a true hold-up style disadvantaged in this shape makes this a low-probability but highest-upside outcome. The market move on race day would be the only reliable trigger for this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Idaho Expresso's ability to sustain front-running — if this horse fades after duelling with Speisialta, the entire pace dynamic collapses and Speisialta inherits a soft lead, dramatically changing the shape and the winners.

Sea Feliz for any market move on raceday — a W P Mullins/Danny Mullins combination with one quiet debut run is a classic Irish maiden pattern, and significant support would upgrade this horse from outsider to genuine contender.

An Lachin Beag returning after 223 days — watch the paddock for any signs of freshness or lack of condition; if fit, the prominent style and Good-ground form make this one of the better-placed horses tactically in the field.
Maroel is a complete unknown and should be monitored in the betting; any market move from a 7lb claimer on a debutant in a field this open could indicate stable confidence that no form can reflect.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Circus Hill, Kilgharrahs Love, Glendaars Crystal, I Dont Really Care) all competing for rear positions means early traffic and potential interference is elevated — watch for any horse caught wide or checked on the first circuit at Sligo's tight bends.

races.name: Kilcawley Construction Rated Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Won twice in last five at 18f on Good ground and arrives just 16 days fresh with Josh Williamson claiming 5lb — the prominent style and course-trip profile make this horse the one to assess most seriously off the pace of Crystabel.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners this well-travelled 5yo who won at 18f on Good last time out; prominent racing style slots neatly into the predicted shape and the 1W7P placing record underlines consistency, though the softer-ground runs in the form string are worth noting.

runners_data.name: Firebrand
runners_data.note: John J Nallen's 6yo has placed twice at 16f on Good and is a natural prominent racer — the redistribution to hold-up on this map reflects the crowded front sector, not its true inclination, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.87 should temper confidence if this horse cannot secure its preferred berth.

runners_data.name: Crystabel
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, returning after 16 days off in the Ryan yard with Danny Mullins up; nine runs on similar ground with one win and five places tells you she handles this surface well and will control the tempo without needing to be pressured into it.

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: Recent form of 8-9740 is modest and the horse arrives just 8 days after its last run; its true nature is that of a prominent racer but it is shown further back on the map because the prominent berths are already filled — the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and poor recent figures make it hard to construct a winning scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Crystabel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, in a field of just five, will dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front without meaningful pressure from any rival willing to take her on. Manoir De Mirande and Luker's Tipple are the natural prominent types who will sit close in behind, creating a compact, orderly race shape rather than a contested pace battle. Firebrand and Hillhead Runner are true prominent types but the field is already crowded in that sector — Hillhead Runner in particular is redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning one or both will be forced to race in a slightly more restrained role than ideal. The race shape will favour horses who can travel prominently in Crystabel's slipstream and produce a clean jump at the final hurdles — Manoir De Mirande and Luker's Tipple are best placed to exploit that position, and prominent hold-up profiles sitting just off the pace are the clear tactical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crystabel Leads, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Crystabel bowls along at a fair clip and one of the prominent pair tracks her into contention entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Crystabel sets a sustainable gallop on Good ground where she has placed five times in similar conditions, and Manoir De Mirande or Luker's Tipple, travelling handily throughout, picks her off after the last with a clean jump.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Crystabel Pins Rivals Back
scenarios.trigger: If the strong ORs of the prominent horses see connections restrain them further than expected, Crystabel kicks clear and holds on.
scenarios.body: With the gap to the field widening slightly from two out on Good ground that suits front-runners who can stride out, Crystabel's 1W5P record at similar trips and conditions proves enough to hold the challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Crystabel gallops too freely early and the pace is stronger than it appears, a horse sitting off the pace gets a soft lead to close.
scenarios.body: Hillhead Runner, though racing out of its natural prominent role with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and a recent form string of 8-9740 that inspires little confidence, is the notional beneficiary, but this scenario is discounted given no genuine hold-up type exists in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tightly Contested Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race is compressed turning in and all five runners arrive at the last hurdle within two lengths of each other.
scenarios.body: A scrappy, tactical sprint to the line benefits the most nimble jumper at the final flight, and Manoir De Mirande's two recent wins at 18f on Good going make him dangerous in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Crystabel (Mullins) could dictate entirely unchallenged — watch whether any of the prominent types attempt to close early, because if none does, she may steal a march that proves impossible to peg back from the second-last.

Hillhead Runner returns just 8 days after its last outing — monitor its freshness and jumping at the early hurdles, as a novice error from an already out-of-position runner could compromise what little chance it holds.

Firebrand's redistribution means it may attempt to push forward despite the map showing it at the rear — watch for a wide or awkward passage as it tries to recover its natural prominent position in a compact five-runner field.

Manoir De Mirande carries headgear (hg:t) and is in the hands of a 5lb claimer — watch whether the combination of gear and inexperienced pilot causes any keenness or jumping errors at hurdles early in the race.

races.name: SIS Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Go To Town
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on a consistent handicap mark of 99; six wins at similar distances on Good ground and a 25-day turnaround suits, though an 0 from 9 on similar going is a concern hidden within that sim-going record — placed form is absent too, suggesting he finds ways to finish mid-pack.|
runners_data.comment: Rated 105 and ranked third of 19, Go To Town brings solid claims having run over today's going before, and 25 days since his last start leaves him fresh and ready; yet winless in his last five starts, and a trainer without a winner in 27 attempts over the past fortnight is a concern.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with strong placed form (6 places from 15 Good-ground runs) who travels prominently and handles this course configuration well; the 35-day break is manageable but age and a long losing run at OR 98 temper expectations.|
runners_data.comment: General Clermont heads the ratings and brings distance-and-going experience to the table, but his recent form gives pause — a fourth three starts back is the best he can show in his last five, and he arrives yet to win in that spell. Fresh enough on 35 days off, the 167 lb burden is the key test.

runners_data.name: Justicialism
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator with an excellent recent record of placed finishes (five seconds/thirds in last five outings) and a sharp 15-day turnaround; the amateur 5lb claimer is a factor to weigh but the horse's consistency on Good going makes it a genuine threat in a compressed finish.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed performer who has been runner-up three times in recent starts, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour — the main risk is he remains winless and that fifth last time out raises a question mark.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer fitted with tongue-strap who has placed three times on Good ground at similar distances; the 7lb claimer and a tendency to need things to fall right means this horse's chance is best if the field fans wide in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and fourth two starts back, Phoenix Arizona has experience over today's trip and going, though winless in his last five starts; at 162 lb, the weight is a further hurdle for a gelding who finds himself ranked eighth of nineteen.

runners_data.name: Andyourbirdcansing
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing gelding who scored at 20f on Good going most recently and holds strong course-distance form with a 14 from 15 Good-ground record; the 5lb claim for Kenneally is a notable booking and the fitness angle after 25 days looks straightforward.|
runners_data.comment: Andyourbirdcansing won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her some grounding for conditions, but her record in recent starts shows that win is the exception rather than the rule, and 160 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Il Pirata
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent type who has struggled to land a blow at 16f on Good ground (0 wins, 0 places from 4 similar runs); the step up to 18f here may suit slightly but the consistent mediocrity at this level is hard to overlook.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and yet to make a meaningful mark in recent outings, Il Pirata at least has going experience to call on; carrying 160 lb looks the stiffest hurdle, and a brought-down run skews the form picture somewhat.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Prominent, versatile performer who ran only six days ago and carries conditions form that reads well on this going (3 wins from 15 Good-ground runs); the quick turnaround is the primary query but Sligo's sharp track suits horses who travel handy.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last four starts, Steps In The Sand does bring a third last time out and has run over today's trip and conditions before, but a hefty 160 lb and a trainer firing at just 5% in the past fortnight are real negatives to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Mon Sheriffe
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse fitted with hood who has pulled up or unseated in recent outings; the trainer has one winner from 26 attempts in the last 14 days and the horse's record of unfinished races is a significant concern in an already crowded field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — a record featuring two pull-ups and an unseating — Mon Sheriffe's profile is patchy at best, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a 13-day turnaround keeps him fresh; the 157 lb burden is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Moulane West
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran with a tongue-strap and boots who has been 58 days off the track; 1 win and 3 places from 13 Good-ground runs suggests ability still lurks, but a hold-up style in a 19-runner race with forced midfield traffic is not ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and yet to show his best on this return from a 58-day absence, Moulane West does at least bring distance and going experience to the table; our rating of 97 suggests more ability than recent efforts imply, but 157 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse who won at 18f on Good going three runs back and has placed 4 times from 13 Good-ground starts; trainer Gilligan has had one winner in the last 14 days and this lightly-raced youngster is improving, making it one of the more interesting hold-up runners.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has been off the mark since, finishing ninth last time out; she has experience of today's trip and going, though carrying 156 lb against a wide field makes improvement hard to pinpoint.

runners_data.name: Copper Rocker
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up runner with a tendency to fade in the finish — highlighted by a repeated pattern of going 0/11 from 6 similar-going runs; Danny Mullins in the saddle is the main positive but the horse has not threatened in any of five most recent outings.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Copper Rocker carries 155 lb for a trainer without a winner in 27 attempts over the past fortnight; experience over today's trip and going offers the only genuine crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Boltlander
runners_data.note: Has genuine hold-up tendencies and wears a tongue-strap, but the map pushes this horse into midfield given the volume of rear-runners; five blank runs including three pulled-ups and a 62-day break make it hard to identify a winning angle, and racing out of its natural position compounds the difficulty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and pulled up three times in his last five outings, Boltlander makes little appeal on these figures — ranked 14 of 19 — though he has run over today's going before and returns after 62 days off.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the 6th-to-10th range on Good ground (9 from 10 runs on similar going) but has never won or placed in those conditions; though a natural hold-up runner, the congested midfield role it is forced into here reduces what is already a thin winning case.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Frontier Rose does arrive with going experience on her side and a 25-day break that suggests she's fresh; however, her recent string of poor finishes and a hefty 153 lb burden make it hard to fancy her strongly from 11th in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Nothing Da Now
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has been absent for 206 days — the longest layoff in the field by some margin — and whose form profile is built almost entirely on Heavy/Soft ground where it has managed only 2 from 6; the big break combined with entirely unsuitable Going makes this a very speculative runner.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a pull-up — and returning after 206 days off carrying 152 lb, Nothing Da Now faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip before, but ranked 17th of 19 on our figures, it's hard to make a compelling case.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood and won at 17f on Good ground two runs ago under this yard (Hogan has 2 wins from 31 in 14 days); while a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into midfield, a relatively light weight and recent winning evidence mean it retains a sliver of each-way interest if gaps open.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up twice in recent starts and finished eighth last time out, Backinabit makes him hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and some experience over today's trip and going; ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, he faces a stiff task at 147 lb.

runners_data.name: Glenriver
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap runner who has not finished better than 9th in five completed runs and recorded three consecutive pulled-ups before that; despite being forced into a midfield slot on the map, this horse's true rear-running style and modest form mean it is hard to include in any winning scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and with three pull-ups among them, Glenriver arrives on a deeply concerning profile; he has run over today's trip and going, but those pull-ups cast a long shadow over his chance here.

runners_data.name: Stormy Jenn
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old fitted with a hood whose best result was a 3rd on Heavy ground at 16f — wholly different conditions to today; the horse naturally wants to come from the rear and the congested midfield role on a Good-ground 2m2f hurdle does not play to any identifiable strength.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, Stormy Jenn's recent form makes grim reading — unplaced last time, a fall and a pull-up before that, though a third four starts back shows she can complete and she has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ripsnorter
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the race, uncontested and able to dictate fully from flag fall; has won over 16f on Good ground and run respectably at this trip, and a 16-day turnaround for Lanigan's yard is fine — the key question is whether a solo leader carrying 168lbs can sustain the effort when the prominent horses arrive at his quarters.|
runners_data.comment: Ripsnorter landed a win four starts back and was third five starts back, and our rating of 108 marks him out as a serious threat here; the worry is that his last three runs have all disappointed, so he must bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood, six-year-old mare with a deeply uninspiring form profile including a 17th of 17 on Soft and multiple unplaced efforts; though she is a true hold-up horse, the map slots her into midfield and neither her form nor her style position gives a clear path to the frame.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a pulled-up effort among them, Lady Victrix heads here ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, and a trainer striking at just 4% adds little encouragement — she has run over today's going before, but that's slim consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Ripsnorter is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead in a 19-runner field at Sligo, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, self-regulated gallop over 2m2f on Good turf. The prominent quartet of Go To Town, General Clermont, Andyourbirdcansing, and Steps In The Sand will track closely behind, likely occupying the first four to six positions and ensuring the pace is honest without becoming a true test of stamina. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Boltlander, Frontier Rose, Nothing Da Now, Backinabit, Glenriver, Stormy Jenn, and Lady Victrix are all genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield positions they would not naturally choose, meaning the true back of the field will be congested and those runners will struggle to find clear daylight when it matters. With one front-runner dictating a steady-to-honest pace and a cluster of prominent horses hunting him down from early, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — they will get a comfortable lead-tracking position, save ground on the Sligo circuit, and be poised to pounce at the second-last without having to produce a long sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter controls from the front and prominent runners Go To Town, General Clermont, and Andyourbirdcansing track closely throughout without a seriously disruptive pace injection.
scenarios.body: Ripsnorter sets a measured tempo and the prominent stalkers conserve energy rounding the final bend before deploying their finishing kicks from ideal positions at the second-last hurdle; this scenario rewards horses who race within a length or two of the leader and can sustain their effort to the line on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Sticks On
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter, uncontested and unhurried in front, sets fractions slow enough that no challenger can close the gap off a truly sedate gallop.
scenarios.body: With no rival applying early pressure, Ripsnorter builds a cushion and dictates throughout, leaving chasers chasing shadows as they struggle to bridge the gap on the flat run-in at Sligo; this shape favours the front-runner who essentially converts a lead into an unchallenged solo performance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the steady early pace causes a bunched finish and one of the genuine hold-up types threads through late chaos in a tightly packed field.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners and multiple hold-up horses forced into midfield roles, the straight becomes congested and a horse able to find a gap and produce a late burst benefits from rivals tiring in front; Justicialism and Phoenix Arizona, natural hold-up operators, are best placed to capitalise if the race compresses into the final hurdle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field causes interference, jumping errors, or forced wide runs that disrupt the prominent horses and open the race to a lower-weighted survivor.
scenarios.body: With riders on amateur and conditional licences aboard several runners and a tight Sligo track, incidents at hurdles could shuffle the pack dramatically; a horse like Backinabit or Georginas Jet, carrying lower weights and racing with straightforward headgear, could benefit from a fortuitous run through a depleted field.

watchPoints.text: Ripsnorter sets the entire tempo alone — if the early gallop is unusually slow, watch for prominent horses like Andyourbirdcansing or Go To Town to press forward earlier than expected and force a change in race shape at the halfway point.

With 19 runners at tight Sligo, the first two flights of hurdles are a significant risk point — amateur and conditional jockeys aboard Mon Sheriffe, Phoenix Arizona, Georginas Jet, and others raise the probability of early jumping incidents that could shuffle positions dramatically.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Boltlander, Frontier Rose, Nothing Da Now, Backinabit, Glenriver, Stormy Jenn, and Lady Victrix — will be jostling for room in midfield to rear throughout; watch for any of them becoming trapped on the rail entering the final bend as the field fans wide.

Backinabit's recent win under the Hogan yard and its light weight of 147lbs makes it the redistributed horse most likely to cause an upset if gaps materialise late — worth monitoring its position at the second-last hurdle.

Steps In The Sand ran just six days ago and is the freshness query among the prominent horses — if it shows any signs of tiredness jumping the last it could open the door for the prominent horses immediately behind it on the final run-in.

races.name: Mulhern Leonard Chartered Accountants Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cut The Rope
runners_data.note: A prominent racer (OR 112) who has run on Good ground before (sim-going: 6/15, 0W 1P) and shapes as the most likely horse to track Ivana D'alco in the early stages; 60 days since last run is a mild concern, and Kieren Buckley will need a positive ride to make the most of this tactical race.|

runners_data.name: Fox Walk
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced five-year-old with an unknown going profile (flagged UNKNOWN) who hops back after 90 days off; his most recent form string (5P3-1) shows progression and Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking, but the trip and ground remain untested questions.|

runners_data.name: Fuusland
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner (T14: 1/44) who has only two relevant form entries at this distance on Good ground with no wins or places from them; a hold-up operator by style, he needs the pace to be genuinely strong to get involved, which is unlikely given Ivana D'alco's control.|

runners_data.name: Minella Moon Shine
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago (LR: 2d) which is an eye-catching stat — connections clearly feel he's fresh enough, and his recent second on Good ground (2/16f/GOO) suggests he handles these conditions; a prominent racer who should sit close to the pace and will be dangerous if that recent run hasn't dulled his edge.|

runners_data.name: Mr Caulfield
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who fades in the finish (flagged) and has one run on Good ground without a win or place; Sean Flanagan's booking adds some interest but the race shape — controlled by Ivana D'alco — is unlikely to suit a horse who needs a strongly-run race to produce his best.|

runners_data.name: San Patricio
runners_data.note: Unknown style (flagged U) with no going data and last run date absent — this is a significant unknown quantity; apprentice Liam McKenna (3lb claim) rides and the Peter John Flood yard has returned 0 wins from 4 runners in the last 14 days, so the angles here are largely blind.|

runners_data.name: Tommy Go Maith
runners_data.note: A hold-up type (headgear: p) who has pulled up in three of his four starts and carries a fades-in-finish flag; the 2m5f trip on Good at Sligo is his longest test and his sim-going record (0W 0P from 2 on similar) does nothing to inspire confidence in this controlled pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Ivana D'alco
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field (tongue-tie, W P Mullins at 17/60 in the last 14 days) who will dictate terms for Brian Hayes from flag to finish; one fall in form (F) and a hurdle-jumping query exist, but on Good ground over 2m5f with no rivals to challenge her for the lead, she controls this race.|

runners_data.name: Turlough Abu
runners_data.note: Elliott's stable standout this race is Fuusland, not this horse — Turlough Abu (OR 82) is a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield slot on the map purely because the rear was oversubscribed; his fading finishes, a STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 racing out of role, and a record of finishing 7th-9th on Good ground make him one to oppose rather than support.|

races.paceDynamic: Ivana D'alco (Brian Hayes/W P Mullins) is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other horse in the field likely to seriously dispute the lead, she will dictate terms from the off at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m5f trip on Good ground. Cut The Rope and Minella Moon Shine are the natural prominent types who will sit closest in behind, likely tracking Ivana D'alco through the early stages at a rhythm she controls entirely. The absence of any genuine pace pressure means this shapes as a truly-run but owner-dictated tempo — no one will rush Ivana D'alco into a war she didn't start. This race shape strongly favours the lead and prominent profiles: if the gallop is steady and controlled, horses who can travel close to the pace and make their move from the second-last hurdle will have a significant advantage over genuine hold-up types who need a proper test to close. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the field can accommodate, with Turlough Abu, Fuusland, and Mr Caulfield all natural closers — Turlough Abu has been redistributed to midfield on the map as a result, but in practice he is a genuine hold-up horse whose preferred race shape is unlikely to materialise here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ivana D'alco Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ivana D'alco leads at a comfortable clip and is never seriously pressured by any rival.
scenarios.body: Hayes sets an uncontested gallop from the front, dictating the tempo throughout and kicking clear from the second-last, with the prominent horses unable to reel her in after jumping the last; Mullins' in-form yard (T14: 17/60) gives strong confidence in a polished front-running display.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ivana D'alco ties up approaching the final hurdle and the horses just behind overhaul her.
scenarios.body: The steady early pace allows Cut The Rope or Minella Moon Shine to travel comfortably in her slipstream and produce a sharp jump at the last to sprint clear; the 2m5f trip on Good ground suits horses who settle just off the pace and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Improver Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to bring the midfield closers into play in the straight.
scenarios.body: Fuusland or Fox Walk, both able to travel within themselves in midfield, close the gap from the home turn if the prominent horses are flattening out; Fox Walk's lightly-raced profile (5P3-1 recent form) leaves potential unexplored, and Elliott's yard represents with Fuusland having shown some ability at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Finish Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the principals or the pace collapses to create a sprint finish that confuses the field.
scenarios.body: Ivana D'alco's hurdles history includes a fall (F in form) and a tongue-tie, so a lapse at a hurdle could bring hold-up types into unexpected contention; Mr Caulfield or Fuusland, both genuine hold-up types, could benefit though their finishing fade tendencies temper confidence materially.

watchPoints.text: Watch Ivana D'alco at every hurdle — she has a fall in her form string and wears a tongue-tie, and any jumping error from the leader would dramatically reshape this controlled race.

Minella Moon Shine ran just two days ago (LR: 2d) — if connections have brought him back this quickly expecting a fitness edge, he could be sharper than rivals expect, but there is also a real risk he is below his best.

Fox Walk (90 days off, going UNKNOWN, lightly raced) represents a significant dark-horse threat from Darragh O'Keeffe — watch the market moves in the final minutes before post time for any confidence signal from connections.

Turlough Abu, Mr Caulfield, and Tommy Go Maith are all genuine hold-up/fading types that the controlled pace will not suit — if any of them are prominent early, it may signal a significantly stronger tempo than expected, reshaping the whole race dynamic.

The Noel C Kelly yard has returned 0 wins from 7 runners in the last 14 days — both Fox Walk and Mr Caulfield run for this trainer, and that strike rate tempers expectations for the stable's pair regardless of individual profiles.

races.name: Lighthouse At Clifford Electrical Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Rated 113 and the class topper in the field, last seen finishing second 21 days ago, but the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 suggests it is operating slightly out of its most comfortable role; if it dominates from the front unchallenged it remains a genuine force, though its three-race spell of finishing outside the frame before that latest second deserves scrutiny.
runners_data.comment: Jupiter Du Gite shaped well when second last time out and has run over today's trip, with our rating of 125 marking him as the pick of nine. Winless in his last five starts, but freshened up on 21 days' rest and carrying 166 lb, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Littlebiggie
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer returning after 52 days off for Ray Hackett, with a record of 0 wins from 5 runs on similar Good ground — the form shows consistent placing without converting, and the yard's T14 run of 0/4 does not inspire confidence about a horse that needs to be at its peak off a break.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Littlebiggie nonetheless posts a figure that puts her second among the nine runners, and her experience over today's trip and going gives her every chance off 165 lb — though that fourth last time out suggests she'll need to find more.

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type who has a clear tendency to fade in the finish (tagged ⚠), has run 10 days ago for the in-form A J Martin yard (T14: 2/10), and found only one win from 5 runs on Good — the finishing concern in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace makes this a difficult profile to place at the head of affairs.
runners_data.comment: Bruant won two starts back and has experience of today's going, arriving fit on a quick ten-day turnaround with his rating of 111 lending solid claims — the worry is he was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three wins from 9 placed efforts on Good ground but recently finished 14th and 8th, and a fall in his form string is a flag; the 8-day turnaround from his last run is quick and the wide-draw type course at Sligo at 2m5f suits those who can settle close to the pace without overexerting.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win in his last five starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but unplaced last time out and carrying 158 lb makes life harder — a mid-division each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type that has posted five consecutive fifth-or-worse finishes on Good ground including two at today's trip — the form string of 155-50 is deceptive given the finishing positions are consistently mid-pack; Shane Fitzgerald keeps the ride and the horse's youth may be in its favour but the ceiling appears modest right now.
runners_data.comment: In The Minus won five starts back and arrives here fit on a ten-day turnaround, with going experience in his favour and our rating of 111 marking him out as a serious threat; the main concern is that unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Lilac Lady
runners_data.note: Won most recently 25 days ago on Good ground at today's trip, carries a remarkable sim-going record of 15 from 15 races on Good, and Alan King (7) comes in for the mount; the prominent style suits a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo and the form string of 53-241 is a classic peaking profile — this is a strong fit for the likely shape.
runners_data.comment: Lilac Lady won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a hefty 156 lb burden tests her stamina and she ranks sixth of nine on our ratings, marking her out as one to respect rather than fear.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride on this hold-up type who has placed twice from five runs on Good going, and the two second-place finishes both came when the pace was genuinely strong enough to set up a late run; the P A Fahy yard is 0/6 in the last 14 days which is a minor negative, and the 30-day absence will require Mullins to place the horse early.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, You Make Me Smile looks hard to fancy at these weights — 151 lb is a serious burden — though she does arrive on the back of two placed efforts and has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type in nature — the redistribution to midfield simply reflects the volume of deep closers in this field rather than any change in how Daniel King is likely to ride it; recent Good-ground form shows a second and a win from six runs, and the John Patrick Ryan yard's T14 of 0/17 is a stark cold-trainer flag worth marking.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into the minor placings last time and third two starts back, Run For The Border has shown some resolve in recent outings, and she has experience of today's going. Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, though, it's hard to make a strong case at the weights.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Serenade
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR89 and a natural closer who has been pushed into the midfield map position due to the crowded hold-up group — its true tendency is to race from the rear, and with a sim-going record of 11 from 11 on Good showing zero wins, this is a horse that competes without converting in these conditions; the 16-day turnaround is fine physically but the form string of 7-0627 offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Whiskey Serenade faces a stiff ask here; a second two starts back offers a crumb of comfort, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but 142 lb makes life no easier.

races.paceDynamic: Jupiter Du Gite is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival likely to challenge for the lead, figures to dictate from the front at a sustainable, controlled tempo over this 2m5f trip on Good ground at Sligo. Littlebiggie, Cornmarket, and Lilac Lady will push to race prominently behind, creating a closely-grouped early order with Jupiter Du Gite pulling the strings. The hold-up contingent — Bruant, In The Minus, You Make Me Smile, Run For The Border, and Whiskey Serenade — will need a strong pace to generate the gaps they require late on, and with Jupiter Du Gite likely to set a measured gallop, that late surge may be neutralised. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the controlled pace, travel into contention at the second-last and sustain their effort on the flat — horses that can organise and finish, rather than those waiting for something that never fully develops. Run For The Border and Whiskey Serenade, although natural hold-up types, have been mapped forward into midfield because the field carries more deep closers than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; of these two, Run For The Border is the more likely to actually secure that position based on recent form profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite dictates an unhurried pace and prominent horses track through unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Jupiter Du Gite sets a manageable tempo that keeps hold-up horses flat and allows the prominent trackers to coast into position from the second-last flight; the horse best able to quicken off that controlled pace from just off the leader wins. Lilac Lady, Cornmarket, and Littlebiggie all profile for this scenario, with Lilac Lady's strong Good-ground form (sim-going 15/15) and recent win making her the standout beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite's front-running tempo proves unsustainable and the field strings out over the final mile.
scenarios.body: A genuine collapse in the early leader opens the race up late, giving You Make Me Smile and Bruant a window to arrive with meaningful momentum; You Make Me Smile has twice finished second in similar conditions and Danny Mullins will be alive to any pace collapse. This scenario relies on the pace being genuinely hot rather than measured, which is against the likely grain given the absence of a challenger to Jupiter Du Gite.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Midrace, Midfield Grind
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling among the prominent group causes interference and the race degenerates into a grinding test of stamina.
scenarios.body: With four horses seeking prominent positions behind one front-runner on a tight Sligo circuit, a compressed midfield could produce scrimmaging and a slowly-run then sprint finish; in a stamina grind, In The Minus's consistency at this distance and Cornmarket's placed form at 2m6f give them residual claims. This scenario suits horses with a mix of tactical speed and staying power rather than pure finishers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite steals a decisive advantage at the top of the home straight and none can reel it in.
scenarios.body: If Jupiter Du Gite's rider Michael Kenneally (5) pushes clear before the second-last and the prominent group have used each other up tracking it, the leader converts; Jupiter Du Gite's OR113 makes it the highest-rated runner in the field and it has finished second last time out. The STYLE_FIT flag is relevant — it is not at its most natural here — but a truly solo front-running display would override that concern.

watchPoints.text: Jupiter Du Gite leads alone and unchallenged — if Michael Kenneally finds a completely uncontested lead through the first mile, watch for it converting from the front before the prominent pack can mount a response.

Lilac Lady's price — her Going record (15/15 on Good), recent win, and style fit for the expected race shape make her a strong profile match; if she drifts in the market, something in the paddock or draw may be known.

Run For The Border's trainer John Patrick Ryan is 0/17 in the last 14 days — an unusually cold spell that should temper confidence in any statistical angles despite the horse's positive recent form on Good ground.

Bruant's finishing tendency to fade is worth monitoring — if the pace suddenly increases in the back straight and Bruant is prominent, the ⚠ flag suggests it will be vulnerable turning for home and could compromise the closers behind it by briefly filling a gap then dropping away.

The four prominent types (Jupiter Du Gite, Littlebiggie, Cornmarket, Lilac Lady) will all want to be near the front on a tight Sligo circuit — watch the early position battle at the first flight, as any bumping or interference could reshuffle the entire midfield order.

runners_data.name: A Chairde Go Leir
